subject: Agriculture
title: GPS-Guided Farming
description: A quick, practical guide to GPS-Guided Farming.

hook.text: GPS-guided tractors drive straighter than any human—within 2 centimeters. That precision saves fuel, seed, and fertilizer.

buildup.text: Before GPS, tractor rows overlapped or left gaps. Overlap wasted inputs; gaps reduced yield.

discovery.text: GPS auto-steer systems reduce overlap from 10% to under 1%. Across millions of acres, savings are enormous.

twist.text: Farmers can work at night, in fog, or in dust—the GPS doesn't need to see. Productivity nearly doubled.

climax.text: RTK GPS corrections achieve centimeter accuracy, enabling the same row to be planted, sprayed, and harvested precisely.

punchline.text: A satellite in space decides where the seed goes. The farmer just watches.

quiz.question: How accurate are modern GPS-guided tractors?

details.summary: GPS-guided farming uses satellite positioning to steer equipment with centimeter-level accuracy. This topic covers auto-steer systems, real-time kinematic correction, and how precision guidance reduces overlap, saves fuel, and improves input efficiency.
details.whyItMatters: GPS guidance eliminates wasted passes, reduces fuel and chemical costs by 10–15%, and allows farmers to work in low-visibility conditions like fog or darkness.
takeaways: RTK-GPS achieves centimeter-level accuracy for planting and spraying
Auto-steer reduces driver fatigue and enables longer working hours
GPS guidance data feeds into farm management systems for season-long planning

faq.question: What is GPS-guided farming and how does it work?
faq.answer: GPS-guided farming uses satellite signals—often enhanced with real-time kinematic corrections—to steer tractors and equipment along precise paths. This eliminates overlap between passes, ensuring every meter of field receives uniform treatment.

faq.question: How much can GPS guidance save farmers in costs?
faq.answer: By eliminating overlap during planting, spraying, and fertilizing, GPS guidance typically saves 10–15% on fuel, seed, and chemicals. It also reduces soil compaction from redundant passes and extends working hours into night or fog.
